Calculator.faq1Q: How accurate are the speed estimates?
Calculator.faq1A: Every speed is a band with a confidence label: measured (a public benchmark for this exact GPU, model and quant), calibrated (a bandwidth model fitted to public benchmarks — ±12% for NVIDIA and AMD cards running a dense model fully on the GPU, ±20% otherwise) or theoretical (±30%, outside our calibration set). Drivers, backend, context and thermals move real results within that band.
Calculator.faq2Q: Can I count two or more graphics cards?
Calculator.faq2A: Yes, as a beta. Pick a graphics card, then raise “{count}”. With an NVIDIA or AMD desktop card, “{add}” also lets you mix in a different card from the same maker. VRAM adds up but memory bandwidth does not, so a model that already fits on one card gets no faster. What you gain is room for a bigger model on the GPUs. When you mix cards, the slower card's share slows the whole run down. Speeds split across cards are all shown as theoretical estimates (±30%).
Calculator.faq3Q: Is my hardware information sent anywhere?
Calculator.faq3A: No. Detection and every calculation run inside your browser; there is no server. A share link only carries the GPU, RAM and settings you picked as URL parameters.
Calculator.gpuConfirmVariant: “{text}”: only one memory size is in the catalog — pick it if it matches yours, otherwise enter your specs below.

Calculator.multiGpuNotice: Multiple GPUs are a beta: we add up the VRAM of {n} identical cards and split the layers across them, as llama.cpp does by default. Memory bandwidth does not add up, so speed stays close to one card. Estimates are theoretical (±30%). Recent llama.cpp builds (April 2026 and later) can be faster with -sm tensor.
Calculator.heteroNotice: Mixing different GPUs is a beta. We assume what llama.cpp does by default: it splits the layers across the cards in proportion to their free memory, and each token passes through the cards one after another, so the slower card's share slows the whole run down. Speeds split across the cards are theoretical estimates (±30%). To run on one card only, pick it in llama.cpp with --device; llama-server --list-devices shows the device names. Ollama puts a model on a single card when it fits there, so its speed can differ from this estimate.
Calculator.extraGpuHint: The calculator mixes desktop cards from the same maker only and leaves out older cards such as the GTX 10 series. You can add up to {max} GPUs in total. Using NVIDIA and AMD together needs another backend such as Vulkan, and we can't estimate its speed reliably yet.
Calculator.singleGpuHint: Fits on the {gpu} alone, and using only that card is faster: {speed}.
Calculator.fitAutoNote: With several GPUs the command leaves out -ngl and --n-cpu-moe: llama.cpp b7410 (December 2025) and later place the experts on each card themselves and keep a little over 1 GB free per card.
Calculator.modelHint: Not in the list? Load it from Hugging Face or enter its numbers below.
Calculator.modelEmpty: Pick a model above to see which GPUs, Macs and CPUs run it.
Calculator.modelCtxClamped: This model handles up to {ctx} of context, so that is what we used.
Calculator.assumeModelMode: Everything in the list uses {ctx} context and KV cache {kv}. For graphics cards we assume a single card, 32 GB of DDR5-5600 system RAM, Windows, and that the card also drives the display. Macs, unified-memory PCs and CPU-only setups use the smallest memory size that gets the best verdict, or the largest when none of them runs the model.
Calculator.mineNote: The list below uses the assumptions shown with the model above, so the same GPU can come out differently from your setup.

Calculator.manualIntro: Type the numbers from the model card or its config.json and we'll calculate the model the same way. This runs in your browser, and nothing is requested from Hugging Face.
Calculator.manualHfActive: While a Hugging Face model is loaded, the thinking mode and maximum context can't be set here. Type a number into any field to calculate your own model in its place.
Calculator.manualParamsHint: In billions. Llama 3.1 8B, for example, is 8.03.
Calculator.manualKvHeadsHint: num_key_value_heads, or num_attention_heads if it isn't there. If config.json has num_global_key_value_heads, use that instead.
Calculator.manualHeadDimHint: head_dim, or hidden_size divided by num_attention_heads if it isn't there. If config.json has global_head_dim, use that instead.
Calculator.manualFullLayersHint: Only for models that mix in sliding-window or linear-attention layers: the number of full_attention entries in layer_types. Leave it empty to count every layer.
Calculator.manualCtxHint: Pick the step closest to max_position_embeddings in config.json, or Not sure.
Calculator.manualThinkingHint: Tick this if the model card mentions a thinking mode. The speed thresholds are then 1.5× stricter.
Calculator.manualActiveHint: The parameters used for each token. Qwen3-30B-A3B, for example, is 3.3.
Calculator.manualExpertsHint: num_experts. Some models call it num_local_experts or n_routed_experts.
Calculator.manualIntegerRange: Enter a whole number between {min} and {max}.
Calculator.manualActiveTooSmall: With these expert counts, active parameters must be at least {min}B.
Calculator.manualActiveTooLarge: Active parameters must be smaller than the total.
Calculator.manualTopKTooLarge: Must be smaller than the number of experts.
Calculator.manualTopKNoRoom: Too close to the number of experts to calculate. Check num_experts_per_tok.
Calculator.manualReady: Your custom model is shown first in the results.
Calculator.manualReadyModelMode: The GPU list below is for the model you entered.
Calculator.manualRestore: Bring back the values you entered
Calculator.manualNote: Models you enter are theoretical estimates (±30%). File sizes are estimated from the parameter count and the bits per weight of each quant. Against the models in our list, dense models came within 9% of the real files, but MoE models were off by as much as 34%. The KV cache uses the layer counts you entered. Models with kv_lora_rank in config.json (MLA, as in DeepSeek V3) store the KV cache differently, so numbers entered by hand can't calculate them correctly. Unless you tick the thinking mode, the stricter thresholds for thinking models aren't applied.
Calculator.hfTryManual: You can also enter the model's numbers below.

CalculatorStatic.startIntro: For six common setups, here is the model the calculator lists first in each size class. Pick that hardware above and turn on only that size filter, and you get the same card. Popular models come first on several setups, so you can compare how the same model runs on each one. Each setup also shows the largest model that fits entirely on its GPU.
CalculatorStatic.startAssume: Each graphics card is assumed to be the only GPU in the PC and to drive the display, with {ram} GB of DDR5-5600 system RAM and {os}. Every setup uses {ctx} context and an f16 KV cache, the same as our GPU pages.
CalculatorStatic.startGood: {good, plural, one {# of {total} models runs great or well.} other {# of {total} models run great or well.}}
CalculatorStatic.startNone: {models, plural, =1 {the only model this size} other {all # models this size}}
CalculatorStatic.startLowerQuant: {count, plural, one {# of them runs with a lower quant.} other {# of them run with a lower quant.}}
CalculatorStatic.startLargest: Largest model that fits entirely on the GPU
CalculatorStatic.readIntro: Pick your GPU, Mac chip or CPU above, or enter its specs by hand. Every model in the catalog then gets a card. Models that run great or well come first: the largest size class first, and the more popular model first within a class.
CalculatorStatic.readVerdict: How usable the model is on that hardware, judged on the {quant} file. A model without that file is judged on its closest file ({alt} for gpt-oss). “Runs great” means the answer comes faster than you can read it, and “Won't run” means the model doesn't fit or is too slow to use. The thresholds for all four levels are below.
CalculatorStatic.readQuant: The GGUF file to download. It's the file the verdict is based on, unless that one won't run. Then the card switches to the file that runs best.
CalculatorStatic.readSpeed: How fast the answer is written, in tokens per second. It comes as a range with a confidence label, and the FAQ below explains the labels.
CalculatorStatic.readMemory: The first number is what the model uses: its weights, its context and working buffers, plus what the OS keeps for the display when the card drives one. The second number is all of the VRAM on a graphics card. On a Mac or another unified-memory PC, it is the share we expect the GPU to use, {pct}% of memory. That's why a model that fits in the installed memory can still end up on the CPU only. When part of the model stays in system RAM, that amount is shown as well.
CalculatorStatic.readModeFullGpu: the whole model is in the graphics card's memory (VRAM).
CalculatorStatic.readModeFullUnified: the whole model is on the GPU of a Mac or another unified-memory PC.
CalculatorStatic.readModePartialOffload: the model is split between the GPU and system RAM.
CalculatorStatic.readModeCpuMoe: the MoE experts that don't fit in VRAM stay in system RAM.
CalculatorStatic.readModeCpuOnly: the CPU does all the work. On a Mac or another unified-memory PC, this is what we assume when the model is bigger than the GPU's share of memory.
CalculatorStatic.readMaxCtx: The longest context that keeps the same verdict and the same placement.
CalculatorStatic.readDetails: The page for that model on that GPU, with every quant, a context-length table and the commands for Ollama and llama.cpp.
CalculatorStatic.readDefaults: The calculator starts from the same conditions as the examples above. Macs and other unified-memory machines start at their largest memory option. Change anything that differs from your machine.
CalculatorStatic.readModelMode: Shopping for hardware instead? Switch to “{mode}” and pick a model to see which GPUs, Macs and CPUs run it, along with the cheapest GPU by street price that runs it great or well.

GuideData.gridCaption: Verdicts at 8k context with an f16 KV cache, assuming 32 GB of DDR5 system RAM and Windows on PCs (unified-memory machines: the memory size shown in the cell). Speeds are estimates with an error band and a confidence label.
GuideData.tierCaption: How many of our {total} catalog models each card runs, by verdict (8k context, f16 KV cache, 32 GB DDR5 system RAM)
GuideData.memoryCaption: Memory a model needs at {ctx} context: file of the default quant + f16 KV cache + compute buffer
GuideData.memoryCaptionGpu: Graphics card memory a model needs at {ctx} context: weights of the default quant loaded on the GPU + f16 KV cache + compute buffer
GuideData.memoryNote: On a graphics card the OS also keeps some VRAM (about 0.6 GB on a Windows display GPU); on unified memory CanRun counts about 70% as usable by the GPU (the real limit depends on the system, and the macOS default is higher).
GuideData.memoryNoteGpu: On a graphics card the OS keeps some VRAM (about 0.6 GB on a Windows display GPU). llama.cpp keeps the input embedding table in system RAM and does not load an MTP block by default, so the weights here are a little smaller than the file; a Mac counts the whole file.
GuideData.kvCaption: KV cache per model: bytes per token (from each model’s config) and f16 KV cache size by context length
GuideData.kvNote: A dash means the context is longer than the model supports. q8_0 and q4_0 KV caches take about 54% and 29% of the f16 size.
GuideData.ladderCaption: {model} on the {gpu}: verdict by quantization (8k context, f16 KV cache)
GuideData.ctxCaption: {model} on the {gpu} ({quant}): memory and verdict by context length and KV cache type
GuideData.unifiedCaption: How many of our {total} catalog models each configuration runs, by verdict (8k context, f16 KV cache)
GuideData.breakdownCaption: Where the memory goes: {model} ({quant}) on the {gpu}
GuideData.theoreticalNote: Theoretical estimates (±30%) mark setups whose real speed varies a lot, such as MoE experts kept in system RAM. There we assume as many experts as fit stay on the GPU and only the rest sit in RAM.
GuideData.colBaselineGpu: Default quant, weights on the GPU
GuideData.colLargestFullGpu: Largest model that fits on the GPU alone
GuideData.factOllamaDefaultCtx: Ollama picks its default context length from the GPU memory it finds: 4k tokens below 24 GiB, 32k tokens from 24 to 48 GiB, and 256k tokens at 48 GiB or more
GuideData.factOllamaKvCacheType: Ollama quantizes the KV cache only when the server starts with OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE (f16, q8_0 or q4_0) and flash attention on; the setting applies to every model the server runs

Common.estimateNotice: Speeds are estimates from memory bandwidth, calibrated against public benchmarks, and each one comes with an error band and a confidence label. Real results vary with drivers, backend, context length and thermals.
Common.speedMeasured: {est} tok/s measured at {ctx} context ({n, plural, one {# run} other {# runs}}; 8k estimate {estEst} tok/s, {estLow}–{estHigh}, {label})
Common.reasoningNote: Models with a thinking mode spend extra tokens thinking, so their speed thresholds are 1.5× stricter (30 / 12 / 3 tok/s). With thinking turned off, a model may do one grade better.
Common.krwNote: KRW figures are rough conversions of US prices at the {date} exchange rate (1 USD = {rate} KRW) and can differ from prices in Korea.

Verdict.legendS: Fully on the GPU at 20 tok/s or more
Verdict.legendA: Fully on the GPU at 8–20 tok/s; MoE experts in system RAM at 20 tok/s or more; or at least 90% on the GPU at 8 tok/s or more
Verdict.legendB: 2–8 tok/s; CPU-only; less than 90% on the GPU; or MoE experts in system RAM below 20 tok/s
Verdict.legendF: Does not fit, or under 2 tok/s

Confidence.measured: {n, plural, one {measured (# run, {ctx} context)} other {measured (# runs, {ctx} context)}}

VerdictReason.capCpuOnly: CPU inference — capped at Runs slowly

Faq.modelCheapNone: No GPU with a current street price reaches Runs great or Runs well at {quant}. The best tracked option is {gpu}: {verdict}.
Faq.modelCardsQ: Can {model} run on an 8 GB, 16 GB or 24 GB GPU?
Faq.modelVramOnly: At {quant} the file is {size} GB; with 8k context a graphics card needs about {need} GB (weights {gpu} GB, KV cache {kv} GB, compute buffer {buffer} GB).
Faq.modelVramOffGpu: Part of the file stays off the graphics card: llama.cpp keeps the input embedding table in system RAM. A Mac counts the whole file, so it needs a little more.
Faq.modelVramOffGpuMtp: Part of the file stays off the graphics card: llama.cpp keeps the input embedding table in system RAM and loads the MTP block only when MTP is turned on. A Mac counts the whole file, so it needs a little more.
Faq.modelVramOffGpuMtpUnused: Part of the file stays off the graphics card: llama.cpp keeps the input embedding table in system RAM and does not use this model’s MTP (multi-token prediction) block yet, so it never loads it. A Mac counts the whole file, so it needs a little more.
Faq.modelCheapWellToo: Cheaper and still Runs well: {gpu} at {price} (street price as of {date}), {speed}.
Faq.modelCheapWellOnly: No priced GPU runs it great; the cheapest that runs it well is {gpu} at {price} (street price as of {date}), {speed}.
Faq.comboRunA: {sentence} {quant} needs {need} GB at 8k context; this setup has {usable} GB of usable memory and {ram} GB of free system RAM.
Faq.comboRunAUnified: {sentence} {quant} needs {need} GB at 8k context; the GPU can use {usable} GB of the unified memory.
Faq.comboRunACpu: {sentence} {quant} needs {need} GB at 8k context out of {ram} GB of usable RAM.
Faq.comboCtxQ: How much context can {model} use on the {gpu}?
Faq.comboCtxA: At {quant} the verdict stays {verdict} up to {ctxF16} context with an f16 KV cache ({kvF16} GB of KV) and up to {ctxQ8} with a q8_0 KV cache ({kvQ8} GB). The model supports up to {maxModel}.
Faq.comboCtxNoneA: No context length fits: even at 4k, {quant} needs {need} GB against {usable} GB of usable memory.
Faq.comboCtxTooSlowA: {quant} fits up to {ctxF16} context with an f16 KV cache ({kvF16} GB of KV) and up to {ctxQ8} with a q8_0 KV cache ({kvQ8} GB), but generation is too slow to use at any length: {speed}. The model supports up to {maxModel}.
Faq.comboQuantTooSlowA: No tracked quant reaches a usable speed here; the fastest, {quant} ({size} GB), is {speed}.
Faq.comboQuantNoneACpu: No tracked quant runs here: the smallest file ({minQuant}, {minSize} GB) needs {minNeed} GB at 8k context against {ram} GB of usable RAM.
Faq.comboQuantNoneAUnified: No tracked quant runs here: the smallest file ({minQuant}, {minSize} GB) needs {minNeed} GB at 8k context, and the GPU can use {usable} GB of the unified memory.
Faq.comboQuantQ: Which quant should I use, and how fast is it?
Faq.comboQuantA: {quant} ({size} GB) is the recommended balance: {verdict}, {speed}. The largest tracked file that still gets {altVerdict} is {altQuant} ({altSize} GB), {altSpeed}.
Faq.comboQuantSameA: {quant} ({size} GB) is the recommended balance: {verdict}, {speed}. It is also the largest tracked file that gets this verdict.
Faq.comboQuantOnlyA: {quant} ({size} GB) is the only tracked file: {verdict}, {speed}.
Faq.comboQuantNoneA: No tracked quant runs here: the smallest file ({minQuant}, {minSize} GB) needs {minNeed} GB at 8k context against {usable} GB of usable memory and {ram} GB of RAM.
Faq.comboQuantNoneRamA: No tracked quant runs with {ram} GB of RAM; with {hintRam} GB, {quant} reaches {verdict}, {speed}.

Turning on MTP speculative decoding (llama.cpp --spec-type draft-mtp) needs memory for that block plus KV cache for it.

Combo.barNoteMtpUnused: The system RAM share above also counts the {mtp} GB MTP (multi-token prediction) block, which llama.cpp does not use for this model yet, so it errs on the safe side.

Snippet.title: How to run it
Snippet.intro: Commands for the {quant} file. Both tools download from Hugging Face on first run.
Snippet.hintConfig: These commands assume {ram} GB of system RAM (the configuration from the RAM hint above).
Snippet.ramBasis: These commands assume {ram} GB of system RAM.
Snippet.ramOther: For a different amount of RAM, pick it under “{section}” above to see the commands for it.
Snippet.fileSharded: File: {file} and {rest} more shards ({size} GB total) from {repo}.
Snippet.nglAll: -ngl all loads every layer on the GPU.
Snippet.nglFitAuto: With several GPUs the command leaves out -ngl and --n-cpu-moe: llama.cpp b7410 (December 2025) and later place the layers and experts on each card themselves.
Snippet.nglN: -ngl {n} puts {n} of {layers} layers on the GPU; if VRAM overflows, lower it by 1–2.
Snippet.cpuMoe: --n-cpu-moe {n} keeps the experts of all {n} layers in system RAM, which is what this estimate assumes.
Snippet.cpuMoePartial: --n-cpu-moe {n} keeps the experts in the first {n} layers in system RAM; the remaining {gpu} layers with experts keep them on the GPU. This estimate assumes the same split.
Snippet.cpuMoeOom: If loading fails with an out-of-memory error, raise the value to {next1}, or to {next2} if that isn't enough.
Snippet.cpuMoeOomOne: If loading fails with an out-of-memory error, raise the value to {next}.
Snippet.cpuMoeFit: llama.cpp b7410 (December 2025) and later split the model in a similar way on their own if you leave out -ngl and --n-cpu-moe.
Snippet.fa: -fa on enables flash attention (needed for KV cache quantization).
Snippet.kv: --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 shrinks the KV cache to {kv} GB at {ctx} context.
Snippet.ctx: Ollama defaults to 4k context on GPUs under 24 GB. Set OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH when starting the server, or /set parameter num_ctx inside the chat.
Snippet.ollamaAutoOffload: Ollama splits layers between GPU and CPU automatically.
Snippet.ollamaMoe: Ollama 0.30 and later automatically keep part of the experts in system RAM to fit your VRAM. Older versions split whole layers instead, which is much slower.
Snippet.ollamaKv: OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE applies to every model this server runs and needs flash attention (forced on above with OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1). /set parameter in the chat cannot change the KV cache type.
Snippet.ollamaSharded: Ollama cannot pull multi-file GGUFs yet, so use llama.cpp for this file.
Snippet.noFit: No run command: this file does not fit in {usable} GB of usable memory plus {ram} GB of RAM.
Snippet.noFitCpu: No run command: this file does not fit in {ram} GB of usable RAM.
Snippet.noFitUnified: No run command: this file does not fit in the {usable} GB of unified memory the GPU can use.
